## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 (2026)

**My top pick is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**, especially if you want to connect your RV directly to the power station.

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product white background" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="160px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={2}>
    **BLUETTI AC200L**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery · 2,400W AC output</text>
    <title size="xl" color="default">$899</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Listed price in the supplied search results</text>
    <text color="success" weight="medium" size="sm">Best for RV connection and expandability</text>
    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="RV buying guide and listed offer"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

### Why I'd choose it

- **RV-friendly connection:** A 30A RV-style outlet makes connecting a compatible RV shore-power cord easier.
- **Useful capacity:** 2,048Wh can support a refrigerator, lighting, electronics, and other modest loads.
- **Strong inverter:** 2,400W continuous AC output supports many common RV appliances.
- **Long-life chemistry:** LiFePO4 is well suited to repeated charging and discharging.
- **Expandable system:** A useful advantage if you later need longer off-grid runtime.

The AC200L is also included among the leading approximately 2kWh models in the supplied Home Backup comparison. <Cite ref="turn988721view0"/>

## Other options worth comparing

| Model | Listed price | Capacity | AC output | Best reason to buy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | $899 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | RV-style connection |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | $899 | 2,074Wh | 2,600W | Output and battery cycle rating |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $899 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | Lightweight, 39.5 lb |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | $799 | 1,920Wh | 2,500W | Lower upfront cost |

<caption>Prices reflect the supplied October 2026 search results, not independently verified checkout prices. <Cite ref="turn988721view0"/></caption>

### Important: A 30A RV outlet doesn't mean 3,600W

Even with a 30A RV connection, the AC200L's 2,400W inverter limits its continuous output to roughly 20A at 120V. That means you shouldn't expect to run every appliance in your RV simultaneously.

A 2kWh battery also isn't a practical solution for running a typical rooftop RV air conditioner overnight without substantially more capacity.

**Bottom line:** Choose the BLUETTI AC200L for an RV-focused 2kWh setup under $900. Choose the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 if lower weight matters more, or the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 if you prioritize inverter output and battery longevity.

One question would help narrow this down: **Do you need to run your RV's air conditioner, or mainly the refrigerator, lights, and electronics?**
